The beam finds a blast door frozen half-open, its cycle interrupted mid-motion, the gap just wide enough to squeeze through — or for something to have already passed.
A single amber console light blinks slowly in the absolute dark, patient and rhythmic, the only heartbeat left aboard the dead ship.
The light catches a ragged breach in the hull, stars wheeling silently beyond it, cold and indifferent, the void drinking all the warmth.
An alien artifact is fused into the hull plating itself, its geometry wrong, its surface unmarked, as though the ship grew around it.
A strange angular glyph covers an entire bulkhead, carved not painted, frost packed deep into every groove, its author long gone.
Long parallel gouges rake the wall panels from deck to overhead, deep and deliberate, curving away into the darkness beyond the beam's reach.
A sealed containment pod stands upright in the corner, its viewport fogged from within, condensation still beading slowly down the cold glass.
Every screen on the entire wall is dead and dark except frozen on one image — the same face, staring directly outward.
The open airlock yawns ahead, its outer door wide, nothing beyond it but the void and a faint scattering of debris still drifting.
A crystalline growth spreads from the ventilation grille across the deck plating, pale and branching, catching the beam like shattered ice.
A data-slate tumbles slowly end over end in the weightless corridor, its screen still lit, still displaying the last entry ever made.
Frozen foam fills the compartment around a ruptured seam, the emergency sealant deployed too late, the breach winning anyway.
Through a gap in the bulkhead, a vast engine stretches away into darkness, cold and immense, larger than anything the ship should contain.
Boot prints in a fine grey dust lead into the dark and simply stop, no return journey, no scuff of turning, just an ending.
Every handhold along the corridor is bent outward, torn from the wall in sequence, as though something enormous pulled itself along in a hurry.
A child's drawing is taped to a pressure door, crayon on paper, somehow still here, still bright, utterly unexplained among the wreckage.
The beam finds a chair bolted to the deck with restraints still buckled, empty, the straps cut cleanly from the inside out.
Warning lights ring an interior hatch, all of them smashed, the hatch itself sealed from this side with everything available as a barricade.
A logbook drifts just out of reach, its spine cracked, pages splayed open, the last visible entry reading only a single repeated word.
The entire crew manifest is still displayed on a wall panel, every name crossed out by hand except the last one, recently crossed.
A specimen jar sits in a rack, sealed and labeled, its contents unidentifiable, moving faintly despite the absence of any disturbance.
Black scoring fans out from a single point on the overhead, the burn pattern wrong, pointing inward rather than out from any source.
A pressure suit hangs in its rack, helmet sealed, gloves sealed, every seal intact — and completely empty of whoever sealed it from inside.
The beam sweeps across a navigation bay where every chart has been manually erased, every coordinate wiped, destination and origin both methodically destroyed.
A mess table is still set, cups and trays in place, a meal mid-eaten, as though every soul aboard simply stood and walked away at once.
